drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. We have revised the preliminary draft to address the proposed thirty-day closing framework, signing and closing representations, and indemnity scope. Diligence must have an agreed scope and objective completion criteria; we propose reciprocal outside-date termination rights, unavailable to a party whose material breach caused the failure to close. We have not accepted uncapped liability or unlimited survival for the proposed exceptions. Please provide the confirmed transaction particulars, proposed schedules, closing deliverables and your proposed liability limitations and exception language. All revisions remain subject to our client’s approval; unresolved items must be settled before execution.

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur on a mutually agreed date no later than thirty days after signing, subject to satisfaction or lawful waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable conditions. Those conditions shall comprise completion of diligence within an agreed scope and against agreed objective criteria, receipt of required approvals, and delivery of agreed closing deliverables, each to be specified before execution. If Closing has not occurred by that deadline, either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, unless that party’s material breach caused the failure to close. Termination shall not affect accrued rights or liability for prior breach, and the parties may extend the deadline by written agreement.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller shall represent at signing and again at Closing that the financial statements specifically identified in the agreed disclosure schedules fairly present, in all material respects, the Company’s financial position and results for the dates and periods covered, in accordance with the agreed accounting standards consistently applied, subject to expressly agreed qualifications and disclosures. Any representation expressly relating to a specified date shall speak only as of that date. The financial statements, accounting standards, disclosure schedules and any qualifications must be agreed before execution.

4. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations and procedures to be agreed before execution, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from breaches of the Seller’s representations, warranties and covenants and from undisclosed liabilities of the Company attributable to periods before Closing. The definitive indemnity provisions shall specify covered losses, disclosure treatment, mitigation, prevention of double recovery, notice and defense procedures, survival periods, thresholds, caps and interaction with other remedies. Treatment of fraud, title, authority and tax claims, including any exceptions to general limitations and any separate limits or survival periods, remains expressly reserved for agreement. This preliminary clause does not constitute acceptance of unlimited liability or unlimited survival.

Please propose the diligence scope, objective satisfaction criteria, required approvals and closing deliverables. Confirm the intended signing date and whether thirty calendar days is appropriate given approval timing. Any extension or different allocation of termination rights requires client approval.

Please provide proposed caps, thresholds, survival periods and exception language. Fraud must be appropriately defined, with attribution addressed and no exclusion of liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Title, authority and tax claims require separately negotiated treatment; tax provisions should address pre-closing and straddle periods and claims control.

receiver.message_back: Subject to Buyer approval, we propose a 20% purchase-price cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and 24-month survival for ordinary warranty claims; title and authority claims should survive six years with a purchase-price cap and no basket, pre-closing taxes (including the allocable straddle-period portion) should carry the same cap and no basket through 60 days after the applicable limitation period, and Seller’s actual intentional fraud, including through authorized representatives, should remain uncapped subject to applicable law. We accept the reciprocal thirty-calendar-day outside-date framework in principle, but execution remains conditional on confirmed transaction particulars, agreed objective diligence criteria, specific disclosure schedules, approvals and closing deliverables, and separate protection for undisclosed pre-closing liabilities and covenant breaches without application of the ordinary warranty basket or cap.
